items_missed: Never asked "How are you today?" after greeting.

Did not recap the submitted quote form back to the customer even though he said "I just submitted the form and then I got this number" — she referenced the form internally but never confirmed details on file with him.
No zip code collected for either the origin (505 West... Selena, TX) or destination (1325... Rockwall) address.
Never asked about moving stressors/worries ("anything you're particularly worried about with this move?").

No explicit "no hidden fees" pitch (credit card fees, transportation fees, fuel surcharge, assembly fees) — she said items were "already included" but didn't walk through the specific no-hidden-fee list.
Clock section entirely missing — no mention of when the clock starts, the 2.5-hour minimum, or 15-minute prorated increments.
Gave two time/cost numbers (5.5 hrs = $1,341; 4 hrs = $1,038) without explaining which variables (stairs, walk distance, packing time, specialty items) drove the estimate.
No Save Your Ass prep speech at all — no consolidation tips, no "take a carload" advice, no sense-check.
No booking attempt — never tried to lock in the July 29th date despite confirming availability earlier in the call.
No deposit-free mention, no email handoff explanation, and no closing "any other questions before I let you go?" — the call ends with the customer saying thanks and hanging up mid-sentence.
Never used the customer's name ("Uday") at any point in the call.
Insurance explanation covered the $2,000 No Worries coverage but omitted the 60¢/lb baseline liability comparison.
top_strength: Roselyn methodically gathered full move details for both the origin and destination units — bedroom count, square footage, floor/elevator or stairs, walk distance, access concerns, and specialty items like the 65-inch TV — before quoting, and proactively offered a budget-conscious tip (using the customer's own boxes/tape to lower the packing cost).
coaching_note: Add the Clock and Save Your Ass sections before delivering the estimate, and always close with a booking attempt plus a no-deposit/email-handoff explanation — this call ended with two quotes given (5.5 hrs/$1,341 and 4 hrs/$1,038) but no attempt to lock in the confirmed July 29th availability, and the customer's name was never used once during the call.
phone_presence_notes: The call stayed strictly procedural question-by-question intake throughout — no use of the customer's name, no empathy or affirming language ("I totally understand", "great question"), and it ends abruptly without a warm close.
audio_review_reason: Low warmth score (2/5) combined with a heavily garbled ASR transcript and an abrupt cutoff ("Roselyn Pammit: And if?") — worth confirming actual vocal tone and whether a booking/close attempt happened after the transcript cuts off.
